findings.title: Sessions that share a seed have identical colour schedules ("twin blocks"), and neither the block-wise CV nor the permutation null accounts for this

findings.explanation: FACT: Before change 3 (2026-11-24) the seed was base + participant number, so every analysed session of a participant used the same 90-sequence colour order. This covers P001 1103/1112, P002 1111/1124, and P003 1120/1121/1125 (1125 was explicitly run as --session 1). The seed for P002 1125 is not recorded anywhere in the repo. In build_epochs.py the block IDs are '<subject>_<date>_b<k>', so block k from two same-seed sessions becomes two separate CV groups. Leave-one-block-out (within-subject) and leave-one-session-out ("new day") therefore always test a block whose exact colour-by-position sequence is in the training set. The permutation null shuffles each block's labels independently, which destroys this cross-session twin structure. My arithmetic check (python3 -c on the regenerated plans, no EEG): a classifier that sees only the trial index and memorises the majority colour at that index across training blocks gets these leave-one-block-out balanced accuracies on the actual group structure: P001 1.000; P003 0.943 (348 epochs, matching sessions.csv totals); P002 1.000 if 1125 used the session-1 seed and 0.789 if it used the session-2 seed. With distinct seeds per session the same check gives 0.367. INFERENCE: any EEG feature that tracks trial position or time-on-task becomes a proxy for the colour label in this CV, while the null cannot exploit it. Examples are habituation of the VEP across a block, slow amplitude trends, and sequence-history (carry-over) effects, which are identical across twin blocks. That would make both the accuracy and the p-value optimistic. The size of the effect in the real EEG is unknown. Partial counter-evidence: the gray1 control uses the same twin groups and is at chance (controls.csv:2-7). That argues against large background-drift leakage, but it cannot rule out position-dependent changes in the evoked colour response, because those exist only in obs epochs. Note: the pre-registered design (research_context.md:132, a single session with 5 blocks) has no twins, because sequence_plan draws a different order for each block.
findings.impact_on_reported_results: Every within-subject number in methods.csv, the subjects.csv verdicts (P002 44.7%, p=0.001, "유의 (보정 후에도)"; P003 39.4%, p=0.038) and the cross-session "새로운 날" rows of generalization.csv for P001 and P003 (and P002 1111/1124) were computed with twin blocks split across train and test, and with a null that ignores them. Because the magnitude cannot be estimated without raw data, the P002 significance claim cannot be accepted as it stands, and the borderline P003 result may be entirely explained by this.
findings.proposed_check_or_fix: Read the seed column from each *_events.csv (stim_rgb.py:388 writes it) and define CV groups as (subject, seed, block number), so that all same-schedule blocks fall in one fold. Report cross-session results only for sessions with different seeds, or flag them clearly. Make the permutation respect the schedule: apply one shared permutation to all blocks with the same (seed, block), or better, build each null by re-drawing schedules with sequence_plan(random seed, 5, 6, 2) and applying the same draw to every session that shared a seed. Add a control that runs the identical CV with X = trial index or time-in-block only, and another that uses obs features with labels taken from a different seed's plan. These quantify how much accuracy position alone can buy. Rerunning on raw EEG is needed to measure the real effect size.

findings.title: The permutation null shuffles individual epochs, but labels are assigned per sequence (obs1 and obs2 always share a colour), so exchangeability fails and the null is too narrow

findings.explanation: FACT: Each sequence yields two obs epochs about 6 s apart (gray1 obs1 gray2 obs2) with the same true label, and they always fall in the same CV block. Under the null, the exploratory permutation gives the two epochs independent labels. The binomial chance threshold also treats them as independent trials. INFERENCE: obs1 and obs2 from the same sequence are adjacent in time and have correlated EEG, so their predictions are positively correlated. In the observed data both members of a pair are right or wrong together, so the score varies more than the epoch-shuffled null allows. The null distribution is therefore too narrow and the p-values are anti-conservative. Illustration by arithmetic (an upper bound, assuming normality, with null SD back-calculated from subjects.csv null95): for P003 (null SD about 3.5 pp, z=1.84, p about 0.033), inflating the null SD by sqrt(1.5) to sqrt(2) gives p about 0.066-0.096. For P002, p_bonf19 stays below 0.01 under the same inflation. This is separate from cv-leakage-01 and stacks with it.
findings.impact_on_reported_results: The P003 "경계 (보정 전만 유의)" verdict (p=0.038) is probably not significant even before correction once pairs are permuted together. The P002 p-value is overstated but, on this issue alone, likely stays significant. The chance95 thresholds printed by run_within are too low because the effective n is about half the epoch count.
findings.proposed_check_or_fix: Permute labels at the sequence level within each (seed, block) group, as train_svm.shuffle_by_sequence does, so obs1 and obs2 keep the same label, and combine this with the twin-consistent scheme from cv-leakage-01. Alternatively, score per sequence (average the obs1/obs2 decision values). Compute binomial chance with n = the number of sequences.

findings.explanation: FACT: Nineteen pipeline variants were compared on the same outer CV with no nested selection. The pipeline labelled PRIMARY is not the pre-registered ERSP + RBF-SVM model, and it is also the best performer in methods.csv. The additional P003 test uses the variant that scored highest for P003. Bonferroni x19 is applied to the permutation p-values. INFERENCE: choosing the reported model and variant by outer test-fold accuracy is a form of tuning on test data. The reported bAcc values (44.7, 39.4) are the maximum of many noisy estimates, so they are biased upward (winner's curse). Bonferroni corrects the p-value for the 19-way choice but not the point estimate, and it does not cover the extra per-subject choices (EA versus raw, channel set). The repo does not show when PRIMARY was fixed, so the "pre-specified" claim cannot be verified.
findings.impact_on_reported_results: The headline accuracies in subjects.csv and the ranking and delta_pp in methods.csv are optimistic. The P003 EA + 4ch permutation result should be treated as exploratory. None of the stored results covers the pre-registered ERSP + SVM analysis.
findings.proposed_check_or_fix: Report the pre-registered pipeline (train_svm.py on xdf_qc features) as primary. If a data-driven choice is wanted, nest the pipeline selection inside each outer training fold using an inner grouped CV, or build the permutation null from the maximum over all candidate pipelines in each permutation to get a family-wise null. findings.title: Fitted steps mostly stay inside the folds, with two exceptions: per-session EA is computed on test-block trials before CV, and the stacking meta-learner uses an ungrouped inner CV

Exceptions: run_within.py:20 "Xea = rp.apply_ea_per_group(X, ses)" runs before the leave-one-block-out evaluate at :26; the same pattern appears in run_extra.py:48 and :70 and perm_fine.py:19; rgb_pipeline.py:71 builds the EA reference from all trials in the group; rgb_pipeline.py:209 "StackingClassifier(members, final_estimator=LogisticRegression(max_iter=2000), cv=3)" has no groups.
findings.explanation: FACT: Euclidean Alignment whitens each session with the mean covariance of all its trials, including those in the test block, before block-wise CV. StackingClassifier's internal cv=3 is a stratified split that ignores blocks and sequences. INFERENCE: EA is label-free and each block is colour-balanced by design, so the transductive use of test-block trials leaks little or no label information. This is standard practice for cross-session EA, but strictly speaking it breaks fold isolation in the within-subject analysis. In the stacking meta-learner, obs1/obs2 pairs and twin blocks straddle the inner split, so the meta-features are over-confident; this affects only the training fold and never sees test labels.
findings.impact_on_reported_results: Affects only the F7 EA rows (methods.csv:5, 8, 19, generalization.csv EA rows, perm_fine P003 EA test) and the F8b stacking row. The effect is expected to be small, and no headline conclusion depends on it.
findings.proposed_check_or_fix: For within-subject CV, compute the EA reference from training-fold trials only, or recompute it per fold from the test block alone (fully transductive but fold-local). Pass a GroupKFold over training blocks/sequences to StackingClassifier (for example cv=list(GroupKFold(3).split(X, y, groups))), or drop stacking.

findings.explanation: FACT: The pre-registered pipeline reads the LabRecorder XDF with pyxdf, which dejitters timestamps by default. The ML analysis instead reads the BrainAccess Board .db. load_db concatenates the per-block `time` arrays as they are and then reorders every sample with argsort(t). It never fits time against the hardware Sample counter, never checks that Sample is monotonic, and never smooths the timestamps. Each marker is then placed on the EEG by searchsorted on those raw stamps. plan_changes.md:66 records that this Board's LSL timestamps are arrival times, with an interval SD of about 15.7 ms (about 3.9 samples at 250 Hz) and some negative intervals. That breaks acquisition order and scrambles samples locally before filtering; the 30 Hz low-pass only partly hides this. (ii) The sample chosen as time 0 shifts from trial to trial by roughly the jitter (tens of ms). findings.impact_on_reported_results: Every reported accuracy (methods.csv, subjects.csv, generalization.csv) and the ERP figure come from epochs aligned this way. findings.explanation: FACT: The .db path filters each recording as a single continuous array. It does not split at timestamp gaps or Sample-counter jumps, does not reset filter state, and has no startup exclusion. Each epoch is cut as a fixed 840-sample slice (k-70 to k+770). The only timing check tests that the first sample at or after the marker lies within 10 ms of it. Nothing checks that t[k+n1-1]-t[k+n0] equals the expected 3.36 s, or that the Sample counter has no gap inside the epoch. Gap counts are printed in build_cache and then thrown away. Trials dropped by the edge or tolerance check are skipped with `continue` and never counted. load_db silently uses only the first data_ table. The plan (protocol.json, xdf_qc.segments/cut) splits at missing samples, resets the causal filter per segment, excludes the first 5 s of each segment, and rejects trials that cross a boundary. INFERENCE: (i) If samples are missing inside an epoch window, every later sample in that epoch is placed earlier than its true time by the length of the gap, so the time axis is wrong for those trials. (ii) The zero-phase 0.5 Hz high-pass rings for seconds around steps at gaps, dropouts or contact-loss events, both before and after them because the filter runs forwards and backwards. The contact==0 test covers only samples inside the epoch window, and the 150 µV ptp threshold catches only large transients. (iii) Dropouts do happen with this device (plan_changes.md:74). findings.impact_on_reported_results: An unknown share of the kept epochs may be time-misaligned or contaminated by filter transients. sessions.csv cannot show this because neither lost samples nor gap or edge drops are recorded. findings.explanation: Parameter-by-parameter (fact), planned vs ML: band-pass 1-30 Hz causal, reset per segment vs 0.5-30 Hz zero-phase over the whole recording. Notch none vs 60 Hz. Epoch -1 to +2 s (TFR pad -2.5 to 2.5) vs -0.2 to +3.0 s. Baseline -1.8 to -1.0 s vs -0.2 to 0 s. Rejection |x|>60 µV or PTP>120 µV after demeaning on -1 to 0 s, plus 1-s flat std<0.5 µV, baseline-amplitude check, any missing sample and 5-s startup exclusion, vs PTP>150 µV over -0.2 to 3.0 s plus contact loss only. Sorting by jittered timestamps (ba_io.py:54) could reorder samples if the DB times carry the jitter described in plan_changes.md:66. I could not verify this without raw data. findings.impact_on_reported_results: The stored accuracies come from different trials, different filters and different features than the planned analysis would use, so they are not comparable to it. Retention rates in sessions.csv, which drive participant inclusion, are not the planned QC rates.
findings.proposed_check_or_fix: Log each deviation, with its reason and date, in plan_changes.md, or re-run with protocol.json values loaded from config. findings.title: Repeated sessions with identical colour order were pooled although their use is undecided; train and test blocks can share the same sequence order
findings.evidence: rgb-eeg-lab/docs/research_context.md:39 "참가자별 1회 방문"; plan_changes.md:53 "같은 참가자가 본측정을 반복(P02/P002 3회, P003 여러 번)하면서 매번 같은 색 순서에 노출 → 순서 학습·예측 효과 우려"; :55 "2026-11-24까지의 모든 기록은 세션 1 seed"; :56 "미결: 반복 세션 데이터의 분석 사용 방식은 결과를 보기 전에 팀이 결정"; rgb-eeg-lab/scripts/protocol.py:82 "s = cfg[\"seed\"][\"base\"] + n + off * (session - 1)" and :94-108 sequence_plan is deterministic per seed and block. ML: build_epochs.py:38 groups = f"{subj}_{ses[:4]}_b{block}"; run_within.py:16 "g ... = M.block.values" (blocks pooled across all of a subject's sessions); results/subjects.csv:2-3 "P002,3,533", "P003,3,243"; results/controls.csv:2 gray1 control P002 32.1 (chance).
findings.explanation: Fact: by documented rule, every recording up to 11-24 used the session-1 seed, so block b of each repeated session has the same colour order. The ML within-subject CV leaves out one block at a time while pooling blocks from all of a subject's sessions. For P002 that is about 15 blocks over 3 days, against the planned 5-fold CV within one visit. Inference: a held-out block such as P002_1111_b1 has an identically ordered twin (P002_1124_b1, and possibly 1125_b1) in training. Any EEG change that tracks trial position within a block (drift after the rest, fatigue, electrode settling) is mapped to the same labels in train and test, so position could stand in for colour. The gray1 control, which shares the same order and still sits at chance (P002 32.1%), argues against a strong position effect, but it has fewer trials (n=115). Pooling 3 sessions also triples P002's trial count (533 vs 180 planned), which contributes to its significance. The team explicitly deferred this decision until before results were seen.
findings.impact_on_reported_results: The P002 significance (44.7%, p=0.001) and the P003 result rest on a pooled-session design the plan reserved for a later decision, with possible order-related inflation of unknown size.
findings.proposed_check_or_fix: Report each session separately (block CV within one session, as pre-registered). Add a control that permutes labels while keeping each block's order, or train on one session and test on another session with a different seed. Record each session's seed in sessions.csv and wait for the team decision before pooling.

findings.explanation: FACT: For an ideal sRGB display and the CIE 1931 2° observer, the colour values are clearly chosen so that R, G and B match each other and the grey background in luminance, so colour onset would be nominally a pure chromatic change. The repository treats iso-luminance verification as a separate step ('별도'). The session-log template asks for R/G/B luminance only 'if measured', and nothing records a photometer or colorimeter reading. The monitor runs in its own 'sRGB mode' at 50% brightness with unknown gamma and primaries. No colour-vision screening is documented. An untracked file, reports/runs/V02/stimulus_photometry.csv, comes from a script whose docstring says the values are NOMINAL and that the monitor was never measured (research/validation/v02_stimulus_luminance.py:4-6), so it is not a measurement. INFERENCE: Iso-luminance holds only on paper. Several factors can break it on the real screen: a small change in the display's transfer function alone moves the ratios by up to about 5%. The 10° square makes the 2° observer model inappropriate (macular pigment mostly affects blue). Blue is already at channel maximum, so its luminance cannot be raised to compensate. findings.explanation: FACT: The control decodes the upcoming colour label from ERP window means 50–500 ms after gray1 onset. INFERENCE: Sub-threshold blinks, eyelid movements and small saccades, which can vary with how bright or salient a colour looks, would appear in Fp features and in EA-aligned features. Any advantage of 4 channels over 2, which is what RQ2 asks about, could be ocular rather than frontal-cortical. findings.impact_on_reported_results: Any RQ2 conclusion, and any claim that EA plus 4 channels helps for P003, cannot be attributed to neural activity.
